payload.claim: No witness exercises the case where two anchored adequacy findings name the identical probe edit (same file/find/replace). `_probe_adequacy` groups findings by `probe_key` in `by_probe` so that one suite run decides every finding sharing that edit (the design's 'duplicate edits applied once, findings decided together'), but every one of the five new session witnesses (`tests/test_session.py`) uses a 1:1 mapping between findings and probes, so this grouping is never actually asserted. Replacing `by_probe.setdefault(review.probe_key(f.probe), []).append(f)` with `by_probe[review.probe_key(f.probe)] = [f]` (keep only the last finding per probe key) leaves every current test green, yet silently drops any earlier finding that shared a probe with a later one: that finding never gets `apply_probe_verdict` called on it, so a genuinely-surviving concern sharing an edit with another finding would never be promoted to a blocker and never reach REBUT.
